operating_point.platform: CPU (laptop for touched files; CI runners for the suite; GitHub runners, 4 vCPU, for probes)
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a 1 mm sphere of 2000 kg/m^3 (m 8.38e-6 kg); a cylinder 0.5 mm by 3 mm lying along the fall line (the block); mu 0.2 (sphere) and 0.3 (block); dt 1 ms, 100 steps; the node on a half-space z >= 0 (an exact plane), and through the build on a tube of 3.175 mm radius tilted theta about -y; the contact's margin its default (the roughness cutoff, sqrt(2) um) through the build, zero on the node; the frictional sweeps' declared count (FRICTION_SWEEPS_DEFAULT 20 until the sweep-count probe declares per kind)
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: the oracles are fixed cases; the suites (test_friction_suites.py) draw at physical scales in the node's dtype (Hypothesis, never shrunk or filtered)

gate_1_block.claim: a block on an incline sticks for tan(theta) <= mu and slides at g (sin(theta) - mu cos(theta)) past it, at 0.5, 0.9995, 1.0005 and 2 of breakaway, both dtypes

prediction.why: two rims held on a flat, each a single-point problem solved exactly in one sweep; the spike's four-corner box needed 200 sweeps near breakaway, two rims along the slope couple less [inference]

control.plant: mu doubled: a slope of tan(theta) = 1.5 mu slides at mu and sticks at 2 mu

gate_1_block.if_wrong: if the block creeps near breakaway, the two rims' coupling needs more sweeps: the residual and the sweep count say how many
gate_1_block.cannot_discriminate_if: the threshold's two sides are both on one branch

gate_2_sphere_node.claim: a solid sphere on the node's plane rolls without slipping at (5/7) g sin(theta) for tan(theta) <= (7/2) mu, and slips past it with its spin at (5/2) mu g cos(theta) / a, either side of the threshold

prediction.why: a sphere's sliding pair and its normal row decouple (the code read's -0.845 is rolling resistance's, not built here)

control.plant: frictionless: the sphere slides at g sin(theta) and never turns

gate_3_sphere_build.claim: the same through built.run on a tilted tube's floor (the contact's default margin, the roughness cutoff)

gate_4_ledger.claim: friction's loss under its own name is mu N times the slip distance while it slides and zero while it rolls; no gift step; the books close

prediction.unit: |loss - mu N sum(dt |slip|)| / max(expected, m g 1 mm)
prediction.why: friction is booked -dt |l| |u| at the solved slip; sliding |l| = mu N

control.plant: friction's sign flipped (disk_update returns -x): the power guard trips and the numerical column carries -2 dt |l||u|

gate_5_gradients.claim: reverse mode in mu through the run equals the closed form sliding (-g cos(theta) T) and central differences (float64); zero rolling (cannot discriminate there: the trajectory does not depend on mu above its threshold)

control.plant: mu's derivative stopped (lax.stop_gradient on the coefficient)

gate_6_off_the_wall.claim: a body a micrometre above the shrunk wall, its point never held, steps as the frictionless hold does, bit for bit: no friction acts without the contact's own normal force

prediction.unit: largest difference of pose and twist after 20 steps
prediction.basis: derived: no force is taken, so the held twist is the free one plus zero

control.plant: the same body on the wall, sliding: the frictional and frictionless steps differ

gate_7_float32_subus.claim: through the node, a sphere spun on the plane under a glycerol-like resistance at the contact (the spike's R at d_c 0.002: R_xx 5.65e-3, R_x,ry -5.32e-7, R_ry,ry 2.48e-9, R_zz 0.663), at dt/tau 0.001 (0.36 us), mu 0.5: float32's worst |v - v_ref| / (a omega0) is float64's within a factor two, the contact carrying the load

prediction.unit: worst |v - v_ref| / (a omega0), each dtype (float64 3.0e-5 measured on the prototype)

prediction_load.unit: mean contact force over the load, float32, after first contact

control.plant: the gap's rounding band removed (CONTACT_ULPS 0 in the frictional allowance)
control.expected_rate: 1/1: float32's error above 1e-3 (the prototype: 1.5e-2) and the contact under 0.5 of the load

gate_8_multi_point.claim: FL-9 on the tube's floor, driven about its axis, held at two or three points with friction: the residual after the declared sweeps reported each step, and unconverged raised where it passes CONVERGED
gate_8_multi_point.case: the sweep-count probe's screw arm, and tests/oracles/test_friction_multipoint.py

prediction.unit: share of steps flagged unconverged at the declared count
prediction.why: the spike's helix left 837 of 1000 steps above 1e-3 of the contact's change at 20 sweeps, a different measure from the cone residual over the free speed; the share depends on the count the probe declares

gate_8_multi_point.if_wrong: n/a: an estimate reported, the flag's correctness judged by its residual (above CONVERGED iff flagged)

gate_9_sweep_counts.claim: the sweeps to 1e-3 of the contact's change at the 99th percentile per hull kind, through the node's hold

prediction_screw.unit: sweeps to 1e-3 at p99, FL-9 (the spike's helix: 120)

gate_10_power_guard.claim: a planted sign flip of friction is caught by the power guard in every draw of every body (sphere, rod, screw), both dtypes; clean draws never trip it at a converged solve

bits.cases: script A, A0, the hull contact (FL-9, contact 0.5.0 and 0.4.0), the rod, a centre-held body, sphere_settling, W2a's plane and tube near-contact programs; float64 and float32; base 1a81914 and head in one job (bit_compare.py)

controls.one_ulp: a parameter one ulp up: differs

costs.prediction: a frictional sphere's hold about 3 to 4 times the frictionless one's (the spike: 3.5x with the exact 2x2); no cost claim in the PR beyond what node_measure.py measures
